name: Apoliticism
summary: Apoliticism is apathy or antipathy toward political affiliation: the apolitical person is uninterested in or uninvolved with politics, or claims a politically neutral, unbiased position. Historic forms include Epicurean withdrawal from public life for the sake of tranquility, and Anabaptist separation of the believing community from the state. It is a stance about participation, not a programme, so it says little about most policy questions.
scope: Apoliticism as a stance of withdrawal or neutrality, drawing on Epicurus (Principal Doctrines), the Anabaptist Schleitheim Confession, and the modern apolitical or apathetic citizen as described in reference works. It excludes partisan 'centrism' and organised abstentionist movements, and nearly all policy answers are inferred or neutral.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Withdrawal from politics gives no view on health-care provision; adherents are split between indifference and Epicurean self-reliance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is an ordinary party-political dispute that apolitical people decline to take a side on.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Apoliticism takes no side in the market-versus-state contest, so this is a split inference.

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership of utilities is a partisan economic question the stance is indifferent to.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels are a standard partisan fight; withdrawal means no committed position.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are a political actor; apolitical adherents neither champion nor oppose them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Epicurus treats rights as useful compacts, not absolutes, but apoliticism has no property doctrine.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is a routine policy dispute on which the stance is silent.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare cuts are a partisan question; no apolitical doctrine settles it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Economic organisation is outside the apolitical concern with staying out of political contests.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Epicurean value on a quiet private life withdrawn from the multitude (KD 14) implies mild unease with state intrusion, though inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is a culture-war issue apolitical people avoid taking sides on.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech regulation is a contested political question with no apolitical doctrine.

strong-leader.rationale: Apolitical neutrality is wary of political power games, so a leader bypassing gridlock is mildly disliked; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Epicureans avoided politics but accepted the state as a useful compact for security (KD 6, 31), so they stop short of calling it harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is a partisan issue the stance does not address.

empower-police-military.rationale: Security funding is a partisan matter; adherents are split, though KD 6 values security from others.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A moral-political dispute with no apolitical position.

decide-locally.rationale: Apoliticism does not address the level of government; withdrawal applies at every level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not addressed by apolitical withdrawal.

traditional-family.rationale: A culture-war question; apolitical people typically decline to side.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Contested partisan issue on which the stance is neutral by definition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Contested partisan issue on which the stance is neutral by definition.

more-religion-public.rationale: Anabaptist separation favours religion apart from state, Epicureans were sceptical of religion in public life; no unified view.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: A partisan program question; apolitical people do not commit either way.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Academic-cultural debate that the stance does not address.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural politics is not part of the apolitical outlook.

gradual-change.rationale: Pace of change is a political position; apolitical people take none, though they lean to quiet life.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is a partisan flashpoint the stance does not address.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: No apolitical position on international institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is partisan economics outside the stance.

nation-first.rationale: Foreign policy orientation is not addressed by apoliticism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Pacifist Anabaptist strands reject force while Epicurean strands are indifferent, so adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: Border policy is a partisan question outside the stance.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental-economic politics not addressed; Epicurean simple living is only a loose analogy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: A partisan policy dispute; apolitical people neither back nor oppose it.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is outside the stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Apoliticism withdraws from political struggle, and Epicurean tranquility (SEP) discourages turmoil, so revolution is mildly rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: Apolitical people often defer to neutral institutions, but nothing in the stance settles it.

central-planning.rationale: Economic system choice is not addressed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic-system question the stance does not address.

land-value-tax.rationale: A specific fiscal proposal outside the stance.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Partisan tax question with no apolitical position.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare design is not addressed by apoliticism.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is partisan and outside the stance.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property distribution is a political-economy question the stance does not address.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Radical economic change is not an apolitical concern.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary policy is outside the stance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No apolitical position on state-organised bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: The apolitical stance is antipathy to political affiliations (Wikipedia definition), which a ruling-party state would demand people embrace.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Form of government is not an apolitical concern; neutral head-of-state ideals fit some, not all.

democracy-best.rationale: Apolitical people abstain from regime debates and may be split between indifference and apathy toward voting.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct votes demand more political participation, which apolitical adherents are reluctant to give (political apathy).

workers-councils.rationale: Councils make politics a constant mass duty, contrary to withdrawal; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Epicurus rested justice on compact rather than natural rank (KD 33), but apolitical adherents are not committed against rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Anabaptist nonresistance forbids violence in every circumstance, and Epicurean tranquility disfavours it, but strands vary.

war-builds-character.rationale: Epicurean pursuit of tranquility sees war as a disturbance rather than a source of virtue; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anabaptist apoliticism sharply separated Christian communities from the state (Wikipedia, Schleitheim), though other strands do not care.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Schleitheim rejects Christians serving as magistrates and mixing church with worldly rule, so scripture-based law is unlikely to be pursued.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence posture is not an apolitical concern.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Apolitical stance rejects politics as the central driver of life; Gramsci's critique shows it opposes this framing, inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims are a live partisan cause, and apolitical people neither back nor oppose it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are a party-political demand; the sources on apoliticism give no stance on them.

civilizational-union.rationale: Union by shared civilization is a geopolitical project that apolitical sources never discuss.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Epicurean ethics treats each person's own pleasure and tranquility as the aim, though it is hedonism with friendship, not egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Epicurus grounds justice in mutual advantage rather than civic duty, and recommends withdrawal from public service.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Whether nature has intrinsic value is environmental philosophy; Epicurean naturalism does not decide it for apolitical adherents.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is a policy dispute that withdrawal from politics leaves open.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A civilizational critique of industry is an ideological claim apolitical people do not usually make or reject.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological acceleration is a programme of the technology-focused ideologies, not of apoliticism.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is a bioethics question the stance leaves to individuals.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Apolitical people may welcome impartial decision-making, others distrust it; no doctrine.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A private life withdrawn from the multitude (KD 14) suggests valuing private space against intrusion; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Restoration versus progress is a reactionary-progressive divide that apolitical people decline to join.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Apoliticism is defined by antipathy toward political affiliations and being without political bias (Collins quoted in Wikipedia), so judging by results over ideology is natural. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

direct-action.rationale: Apolitical stance withdraws from activism of all kinds, including protest.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative method is an activist doctrine; apolitical people do not engage in movement strategy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivist claims are unrelated to the apolitical stance, although Epicurean simplicity is a faint echo.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A radical economic demand with no counterpart in apolitical sources.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist distribution principle not addressed by apolitical sources.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist economic principle apolitical sources do not take up.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist economic theory that apolitical sources do not take a side on.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejects political domination and revolutionary party politics; inferred from the stance's withdrawal.

collective-farming.rationale: Farm organisation is an agrarian-policy question outside the stance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Leninist thesis in the theory of imperialism, not taken up by the stance.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; Epicurean compacts imply obligations to agreed arrangements.

harm-principle.rationale: Epicurus defines natural justice as a compact neither to harm nor be harmed (KD 31), close to limiting restrictions to preventing harm. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual versus group rights is a liberal-communitarian dispute apolitical sources leave open.

conscription.rationale: Anabaptist nonresistance and Epicurean withdrawal from public duty both oppose compulsory service; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Withdrawal resembles exit, yet apolitical people do not hold this theory of checks.

state-as-business.rationale: A public-choice framing of government that apolitical sources do not address.

positive-liberty.rationale: A debate within liberal theory that apolitical adherents do not weigh in on.

media-academia-power.rationale: A populist claim about institutions; apolitical people may suspect it or ignore it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: A scientific-racial claim with no connection to the apolitical stance.

organic-representation.rationale: A corporatist constitutional scheme the stance does not discuss.

total-state.rationale: A state directing every area of life is the opposite of retreat from politics; Schleitheim also demands separation from civil affairs.

national-rebirth.rationale: Mass political mobilisation for national renewal conflicts with the stance's disengagement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Epicurean tranquility and avoidance of the 'general fray' oppose expansionist striving; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal theory of authority with no bearing on apolitical sources.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is a feudal institution that apolitical sources do not defend or attack.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Apoliticism claims neutrality is possible; the claim that all is political is the Gramscian criticism it faces.

universal-morality.rationale: Epicureans were naturalist hedonists who treated justice as conventional (KD 33), but apoliticism has no unified moral theory.

single-common-good.rationale: Epicurean justice is mutual agreement between parties, not a single reasoned common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A Zionist claim; apolitical people decline to take national sides.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: A nationalist claim apolitical sources are silent on.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist cultural project outside the stance.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy is a social-democratic and socialist aim not taken up by apolitical sources.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding design is a narrow partisan policy dispute.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is a technocratic and partisan matter outside the stance.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is a partisan welfare design question.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: A futurist avant-garde demand with no link to apoliticism.

dominated-front.rationale: An anti-Western alignment doctrine outside the apolitical stance.

workers-nation.rationale: A national-socialist or nationalist labour question the stance leaves alone.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: A culture-war question on which apolitical people decline to commit.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is a religious-economic question with no apolitical doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: No apolitical doctrine; the stance's neutrality does not endorse any such law, but adherents would not campaign against it either.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state is the kind of political theorising apolitical people avoid.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy supply is a partisan policy matter outside the stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Assimilation policy is a nationalist-multiculturalist dispute apolitical people leave open.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracist claim that apolitical sources neither endorse nor reject.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral design is a detail the stance leaves to others.

national-mission.rationale: Missions to spread a government form entail political crusading, opposite to apolitical disengagement.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Claims that structures are political everywhere resemble the 'personal is political' view the stance is criticised by (Wikipedia on Hanisch); inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Antipathy toward political affiliations and alienation from leaders (Wikipedia, political apathy) make distrust of elites a common apolitical attitude. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not addressed by apolitical sources.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice policy is not discussed in the apolitical sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Epicurean justice as security from mutual harm (KD 6, 31) fits a state limited to protecting people, though no apolitical canon says so.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: A racist doctrine unrelated to apolitical sources, which are silent on it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not addressed; Epicurus valued friendship but also had no egalitarian political doctrine.

socialism-one-country.rationale: An internal Marxist-Leninist dispute outside the stance.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: A postcolonial historical-political judgement that apolitical people stay out of.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law policy is a partisan question in some countries and outside the stance.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is a religious-political issue the stance does not address.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-cultural law proposal outside apolitical sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: School religion policy is not covered; the Anabaptist separation strand would only loosely support it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Strengthening a state apparatus is contrary to withdrawal from politics; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Epicurus treats justice as a compact for mutual non-harm (KD 33), which is not a theory of political legitimacy, and apolitical people seldom take a position on it.

trade-surplus.rationale: A mercantilist aim not taken up by apolitical sources.

population-transfer.rationale: Forcibly harming minorities breaks the compact not to harm or be harmed (KD 31); inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Epicurean values of tranquility and friendship regard striving as a source of disturbance; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are a question about political affiliation rules rather than apolitical belief.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of liberty that apolitical sources do not take up.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is a topic apolitical sources do not treat.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined party of revolutionaries is the opposite of apoliticism's antipathy to political affiliations.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A moral-political priority rule with no apolitical source position.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing-policy detail outside the stance.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour-law design is a narrow partisan question.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: A Malthusian causal claim apolitical sources do not take up.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: A contested empirical claim the stance does not address.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is among reforms proposed to counter apathy (Wikipedia), but no apolitical canon endorses it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Epicurean compacts exist to prevent harm to persons, so abuse of the vulnerable is disfavoured; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Emergency price policy is an economic-policy matter outside the stance.
